explanation: Turner Syndrome is a female-only disorder characterized by an XO karyotype, where one X chromosome is missing. It occurs in approximately 1 in 10,000 females. Characteristic features include a broad chest, webbed neck, and small, underdeveloped reproductive organs (ovaries, oviduct, and uterus). Consequently, affected individuals do not undergo puberty or menstruate, though they typically possess normal intelligence. In vitro fertilization (IVF) using donor eggs has allowed some individuals with Turner Syndrome to give birth.
